request.question: Why can pij not treat a live PID or tmux pane id alone as proof that an old attachment survived a reboot, and what does it do when liveness remains uncertain?

ground_truth.search_query: how does pij decide whether a peer is alive or stale
addresses: el:git:github.com/AI-Substrate/pij/docs/how/pij-reboot-rehydrate.md::Coming back after a reboot::"Is that old attachment dead?"
ground_truth.resolution: Address returned ok=true via flowspace3 get at span [73,144].
source_facts: Operating systems recycle PIDs and new tmux servers recycle pane ids, so either identifier can name an unrelated process after reboot.
An uncertain classification blocks writes; revive --print remains read-only, while --assume-dead is an explicit operator override.
A terminal observation of unavailable proves nothing and does not count.
